verses.127:1: {beati} todos os que temem o Senhor, * os que andam {ejus}.
verses.127:3b: Os teus {v3b} {novellae}, * ao redor da tua mesa.
verses.127:4: {ecce} {benedicetur} o homem * que teme o Senhor.
verses.127:5: O Senhor {benedicat} de Sião: * {videas5} {bona} de Jerusalém todos os dias da tua vida.
verses.127:6: {videas6} os filhos dos teus filhos, * {pacem} sobre Israel.

decisions.why: D19 settles beátus → bem-aventurado (29 places; the Latin psalter never says felix). Brazil knows this psalm as 'Felizes os que temem o Senhor e trilham seus caminhos' (the Lectionary refrain for the Holy Family and the 33rd Sunday, Year A) and 'Feliz és tu se temes o Senhor' (CNBB Liturgia das Horas) — both fetched, see circulation.md; both from the Hebrew. The psalm says the word twice (127:1 plural, 127:2 'beátus es'), and the two must stay one word.

options.label: Bem-aventurados … bem-aventurado és
options.note: Draft, by D19; Matos Soares 1932 has exactly these words in both verses. 127:1's first colon runs +4 syllables over the Latin (15 against 11), as 118:1 did; accepted. v2: 127:2 in the natural order, és bem-aventurado (stylist: the inversion is Latinate and "és, e" makes a hiatus at the comma); the Latin order stays as the next option.

options.label: Felizes … feliz és
options.note: The familiar Brazilian wording (Lectionary refrain, CNBB LH, the Diurnal Monástico 1962 'FELIZ'); two syllables shorter. Refused under D19.

options.label: Bem-aventurados … bem-aventurado és
options.note: Draft 1: the Latin order (beátus es), Matos Soares 1932. Changed for the stylist.

decisions.why: The stylist asked for "Pois" at the head of the sentence ("Porque" alone sounds like a clause that lost its main verb). The glossary keeps quia → porque, with "pois" only where "por que" questions follow (D42). The ambiguity reader heard "Porque" as "because" at once.

options.label: Porque
options.note: Draft; the glossary's default, Matos Soares 1932. Kept: the causal link to 127:1 is what the Latin has, and the reader heard it.

options.label: Pois
options.note: The stylist's. Refused as a departure from D42 that the ear did not need (the ambiguity reader had no trouble with "Porque").

decisions.why: The Latin fronts the object before 'quia' ('the labours of your hands, because you will eat'), the Greek's order too (τοὺς πόνους τῶν καρπῶν σου φάγεσαι — the Greek has 'fruits', the Latin 'hands'; the Latin is followed). Portuguese cannot keep the object before 'porque'; the conjunction goes first. 'labóres' is the fruit of toil, and 104:44 already has 'os trabalhos dos povos' for it. 'Eat the labours' is the Latin's concrete image and is kept; the question is only the article or the partitive.

options.label: comerás dos trabalhos
options.note: Draft. The partitive 'comer de' is how Portuguese says eating from a store ('comer do pão'); Matos Soares 1932 'comerás dos trabalhos das tuas mãos'. The plural of labóres kept.

options.label: comerás os trabalhos
options.note: The Latin's plain accusative, as Douay-Rheims 'thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands'. Heard as eating the labour itself — stranger in Portuguese than in English.

options.label: do trabalho
options.note: Singular, as the CNBB 'Do trabalho de tuas mãos hás de viver' and the Diurnal. Loses the Latin's plural for no gain of sense.

decisions.why: An impersonal 'it will be well with you' (καλῶς σοι ἔσται). Portuguese has the impersonal 'ir bem a alguém'. The CNBB's 'tudo irá bem' supplies a subject.

options.label: e te irá bem
options.note: Draft; Matos Soares 1932's words. Impersonal as the Latin; ends on the stressed 'bem'. The pronoun before the verb is the Brazilian placement after 'e'.

options.label: e tudo te irá bem
options.note: More native (the CNBB's 'tudo irá bem'), but 'tudo' is a subject the Latin does not have.

options.label: e estarás bem
options.note: Makes the addressee the subject; a state of health rather than of fortune.

decisions.why: The stylist: with a plural subject "seus" may be heard as "their own ways". The ambiguity reader listed both readings and named "the Lord's ways" as the likely hearing. 118:3 has "nos seus caminhos" for the same Latin.

options.label: nos seus caminhos
options.note: Draft; 118:3's words; Matos Soares 1932. Kept: the ambiguity reader heard the Lord's ways first.

options.label: nos caminhos dele
options.note: The stylist's. Unambiguous, but colloquial at a cadence and it would part the verse from 118:3.

decisions.latin: Uxor tua sicut vitis … Fílii tui sicut novéllæ
decisions.why: Both images have no verb in the Latin or the Greek. Matos Soares 1932 supplies 'será' and 'estarão', the CNBB 'é' and 'são'. A copula is allowed (rule 2), but any copula chooses a tense the Latin leaves open between the future of 127:2 ('manducábis') and 127:4 ('benedicétur') and a timeless picture; Ps 122:2 kept its verbless comparison. The comma after 'abúndans' and 'olivárum' is the Latin's.

options.label: é … são
options.note: v2, the stylist's: a present copula in both members, so the pair stays parallel ("A tua esposa é como videira abundante"). Rule 2 allows it; the stylist named the verbless 3a the worst line of the psalm, and the ambiguity reader already heard the verbless line as a present description — so the copula states what is heard, not a new reading. The present of a nominal sentence is the timeless present in Portuguese; the CNBB has it too. Cost: the Latin's open tense is made present.

options.label: verbless
options.note: Draft 1. A tableau, as the Latin. The stylist: "without a verb the line hangs"; worst line.

options.label: será … serão
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (future, following 127:2). 'A tua esposa será como videira abundante'. Decides the tense.

decisions.why: vitis is the plant (videira), not the vineyard (vínea → vinha, 79:9). abúndans is 'overflowing, rich' (εὐθηνοῦσα, 'thriving'); Matos Soares 1932 and the CNBB have 'fecunda', which names fertility where the Latin names abundance — the reading of the wife as mother is left to the next line, which the Latin also does. The glossary keeps the abund- family on its root (abundántia → abundância).

options.label: como videira abundante
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word kept by its cognate. 12 syllables against the Latin's 11.

options.label: como videira fecunda
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('vide fecunda') and the CNBB ('videira bem fecunda'); the wording Brazil knows. Interprets abúndans as fertility.

options.label: como videira viçosa
options.note: 'Flourishing' — close to the Greek, but a different word from the Latin's.

options.label: como uma videira abundante
options.note: With the article; one more beat, nothing more said.

decisions.why: latus is 'side, flank', of a building its side walls (the Greek ἐν τοῖς κλίτεσι, 'on the sides'); the image the Latin makes is a vine grown along the walls of the house — Douay-Rheims 'on the sides of thy house'. The Hebrew has 'the inner recesses', which is why Matos Soares 1932 has 'no interior' and the CNBB and the Diurnal 'no coração da tua casa'. The glossary already has 'os lados do norte' for látera Aquilónis (D43).

options.label: nos lados
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word, as D43's 'lados'. Risk: 'nos lados da tua casa' may be heard vaguely, 'around your house' — for the readers to test.

options.label: aos lados
options.note: The stylist's ("nos lados" sounds colloquial, "lá pelos lados"). Refused: "aos lados" puts the vine beside the house, where the Latin's "in" puts it on its sides; and the ambiguity reader heard "nos lados" as the outside walls — the Latin's image.

options.label: junto às paredes
options.note: Makes the image plain (a vine along the walls), but names walls the Latin calls sides.

options.label: no interior
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 — the Hebrew's sense, not the Latin's. Refused under rule 1.

options.label: no coração
options.note: The CNBB and the Diurnal Monástico 1962, from the Hebrew; the wording Brazil knows. Refused under rule 1 (and a metaphor the Latin does not make).

decisions.why: novéllæ (plantæ) are young plants, new shoots (νεόφυτα, 'new-planted'). olivárum is plural. The half-verse is also the Corpus Christi Vespers antiphon ('Sicut novéllæ olivárum, * Ecclésiæ fílii sint in circúitu mensæ Dómini', DO Tempora/Pent01-4), so it must read alone. 'Rebentos' already renders propágines at 79:12 (a different word, a different Greek, never in one psalm).

options.label: como rebentos de oliveiras
options.note: v2, the Latinist's (minor): the Latin's plural olivárum. Draft 1's reason for the singular (sibilants) was weak against the Latin's number; the line still reads alone as the Corpus Christi antiphon. The ambiguity reader did not know "rebentos"; kept, as the word Brazil sings in the CNBB text of this verse ("rebentos de oliveira"); "mudas" is the plainest option.

options.label: como rebentos de oliveira
options.note: Draft 1: the CNBB's generic singular. Changed for the Latinist.

options.label: como renovos de oliveira
options.note: 'renovo' keeps the nov- of novéllæ and stays apart from 79:12's 'rebentos'; less current in Brazil.

options.label: como mudas de oliveira
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico 1962: the nurseryman's word, very plain.

options.label: como pimpolhos de oliveiras
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. In Brazil 'pimpolho' is first a nickname for a small child.

decisions.why: ecce → eis (glossary); 122:2a 'Eis que' is the particle's usual shape before a clause. sic is 'thus', pointing back at 127:2–3. Matos Soares 1932 and the CNBB turn it into 'Eis como' / 'Será assim'. The line is the Communion of the Nuptial Mass ('Ecce sic benedicetur omnis homo, qui timet Dominum', fetched) and reads alone.

options.label: Eis que assim
options.note: Draft. Both particles kept, 'assim' for sic; 122:2a's shape.

options.label: Eis como
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal. Idiomatic, but 'como' turns 'thus' into 'how', an exclamation.

options.label: Eis: assim
options.note: The bare particle with the Latin's pause.

decisions.latin: benedicétur homo … Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion
decisions.why: The benedícere (God → man) row keeps 'bendizer' (133:3 'O Senhor te bendiga de Sião', 66:7b, 84:2, 111:2 'será bendita'), open for Gustavo's ruling. The glossary's formula row names 127:5 beside 133:3 as the same blessing (dative here, accusative there — Portuguese 'te' serves both). Brazil knows this psalm with 'abençoar' ('Será assim abençoado todo homem', 'O Senhor te abençoe de Sião', CNBB, fetched); Matos Soares 1932 likewise. The psalm's two places must stay one verb.

options.label: será bendito … te bendiga
options.note: Draft, by the row; 127:5's first colon is 133:3's word for word.

options.label: será abençoado … te abençoe
options.note: Matos Soares 1932, the CNBB, the Diurnal: the familiar verb. Goes with the row, not alone: 133:3 would follow.

decisions.why: bona (τὰ ἀγαθά), 'good things'. The glossary has 'coisas boas' (bona tríbuere, 12:6b; 83:13), and 121:9 'busquei coisas boas para ti', said to Jerusalem, is the nearest place; 26:13 kept 'os bens do Senhor' because the antiphon is known so. 'os bens de Jerusalém' (Matos Soares 1932) is heard first as the city's property.

options.label: os bens
options.note: v2, the stylist's: of two faithful words the plainer and shorter (D2); brings the longest colon of the psalm from 23 to 20 syllables, the Latin's count. 26:13 "os bens do Senhor" and Matos Soares 1932 have it. Draft 1 feared "the city's property"; the ambiguity reader heard "goods" vaguely even with "coisas boas", so the draft's word bought nothing.

options.label: as coisas boas
options.note: Draft, with 121:9 (the same city) and the row. Second colon 22 syllables against the Latin's 20.

decisions.why: A subjunctive of wish, twice, continuing 'Benedícat'. Portuguese can carry the bare optative after a wish ('e vejas'), as Matos Soares 1932 does; 'e que vejas' is the everyday build and one syllable longer. The anaphora (vídeas … vídeas) stays either way.

options.label: e vejas … E vejas
options.note: Draft; Matos Soares 1932. Heard as a wish because it follows 'O Senhor te bendiga'.

options.label: e que vejas … E que vejas
options.note: The ordinary Portuguese wish; one syllable more in each place.

decisions.why: The Latin has the accusative: 'pacem' is a second object of 'vídeas' — may you see your children's children, (and) peace upon Israel. The Greek has the nominative εἰρήνη, a bare blessing, and so does 124:5 in the Latin ('pax super Israël', drafted there as 'paz sobre Israel'). The Latin of the two psalms differs by case, so rule 6 does not bind them to one wording; the Latin is followed here (rule 1). Douay-Rheims keeps an apposition ('thy children's children, peace upon Israel'); Matos Soares 1932 adds 'e a paz'.

options.label: a paz sobre Israel
options.note: Draft. The article makes 'a paz' a second object of 'vejas', in apposition as the Latin has it, without adding 'e'; the ear can still hear the closing blessing. 7 syllables, the Latin's count.

options.label: paz sobre Israel
options.note: 124:5's words: a bare blessing, the Greek's nominative. Loses the Latin's accusative.

options.label: e a paz sobre Israel
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Makes the object plain by supplying 'e'.

choices.127:1: No title line: the Latin of DO has none, and D7 keeps the tituli out (as Pss 119–122, 133). 'qui timent Dóminum' → 'os que temem o Senhor' (113:19, 117:4). The second 'qui' is resumed as 'os que' (118:1's build), with no 'e' (Matos Soares 1932 adds one). ámbulant → 'andam' (row: not 'caminhar' beside 'caminho'); 'nos seus caminhos' as 118:3. The Monastic None antiphon and the Vespers antiphon are the first colon's first words, 'Bem-aventurados todos * os que temem o Senhor' reads alone.
choices.127:2: The singular 'tu' begins here: the psalm turns to one man (rule 3: a singular human addressee is 'tu'). 'Porque' for quia at the head of the clause. manducáre → comer (row).
choices.127:3a: uxor → 'esposa': 'mulher' is heard first as 'woman'. The article before the possessive (rule 5). 3a and 3b are built alike, as in the Latin. The half-verse is the Gradual of the Nuptial Mass (fetched) and reads alone.
choices.127:3b: in circúitu → 'ao redor de' (row; the row names this verse). 'mensa' → 'mesa'. The Corpus Christi antiphon is made of this line.
choices.127:4: homo → 'o homem' (not 'todo homem': 'omnis' is the Nuptial Communion's addition, not the psalm's). 'qui timet Dóminum' → 'que teme o Senhor', as 111:1. No comma before the relative: in Portuguese it would make it non-restrictive.
choices.127:5: ex Sion → 'de Sião', as 133:3 (the ps133 note asked 127:5 to follow). 'ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ' → 'todos os dias da tua vida', 22:6's 'todos os dias da minha vida'. The ambiguity reader heard "O Senhor te bendiga de Sião" as "the Lord of Zion" first; the formula is 133:3's and is left as it is (the Latin's ex Sion is as close to Dóminus); "e vejas" can be heard as an imperative — "e que vejas" is option 1 of videas.
choices.127:6: fílios filiórum → 'os filhos dos teus filhos' (102:17b 'os filhos dos filhos'; the pronoun is the Latin's tuórum). The ambiguity reader heard "a paz sobre Israel" as a second object of "vejas" — the Latin's accusative, as intended.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Liturgical use by grep and Brazilian circulation fetched: circulation.md. Hard readings: 127:6 pacem (accusative, against the Greek's and 124:5's nominative), 127:3a in latéribus (the Latin's sides against the Hebrew's recesses that all Brazilian versions follow), 127:4–5 benedícere (the row's bendizer against the familiar abençoar).

Hard checks pass (ids and marks). Soft flags accepted: 127:1 first colon +4 (bem-aventurados, D19, as 118:1); 127:3a first colon +4 by the heuristic count, ~+2 once esposa‿como and videira‿abundante elide; 127:5 second colon +3 (as coisas boas; os bens is the shorter option); 127:6 first colon -4 (Latin inflections; nothing to add). Oxytone cadences at 127:1, 2, 4b, 5a, 6b fall on Senhor, mãos, bem, Sião, Israel — stressed last syllables, allowed by rule 4.
claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Two minors, no major. 127:3b plural taken; 127:2 partitive refused.

outcomes.remark: partitive "dos trabalhos" for the direct accusative
outcomes.reason: The partitive is how Portuguese says eating from a store — grammar under D2, Matos Soares 1932's wording; "comer os trabalhos" is heard as eating the labour itself. The Latinist called it idiomatic; his wording is option 1.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. 6 remarks: 4 taken (és bem-aventurado; é / são in 3a–3b; os bens), 2 refused and kept as options (Pois; nos caminhos dele), 1 refused as an option (aos lados). Worst 127:3a, best 127:6.

outcomes.remark: "nos seus caminhos" heard as their own ways
outcomes.reason: The ambiguity reader heard the Lord's ways first; 118:3 has the same words for the same Latin.
D42 keeps porque; the ambiguity reader heard "because" at once.
"aos lados" moves the vine beside the house; the Latin has "in", and the ambiguity reader heard "nos lados" as the walls.

outcomes.remark: "as coisas boas" flat and long → "os bens"

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, blind. 11 readings; unknown words "rebentos", "Sião". Nothing changed on its account alone; it decided two stylist remarks (seus, nos lados) and supported one (the copula).

outcomes.remark: "seus caminhos" his or their own; likely the Lord's
description or promise; heard as present
outcomes.reason: The present copula states what was heard.
Kept as the word of the Brazilian liturgical text of this verse; "mudas" and "renovos" are options.

outcomes.remark: "de Sião" heard as "the Lord of Zion"
outcomes.reason: The formula is 133:3's; a reordering would touch both psalms — noted for the glossary row.

outcomes.remark: "e vejas" possibly heard as an imperative
outcomes.reason: After "te bendiga" the wish is heard; "e que vejas" is the option.

outcomes.remark: "a paz" heard as a second object of "vejas"
outcomes.reason: This is the Latin's accusative; the draft stands.

audit.note: v2: 127:2 és bem-aventurado; 127:3a–3b present copula é / são; 127:3b de oliveiras; 127:5 os bens. Two new decisions record refused stylist remarks (quia, ejus). Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json.

v2: hard checks pass. Soft: 127:1 +4 (as v1); 127:3a +5 by the heuristic count with the supplied é, about +2 once tua‿esposa, esposa‿é and videira‿abundante elide — accepted for the copula; 127:6 -4 (as v1); 127:5 second colon now at the Latin's length.

claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Gate clean of majors: one minor, the same as v1 (127:2 partitive), held as option 1 of labores. He passed the supplied copulas, the plural oliveiras and os bens.

outcomes.remark: partitive "dos trabalhos" for the direct accusative
outcomes.reason: Held as in v1: the partitive is grammar (D2) and Matos Soares 1932's wording; "comer os trabalhos" is heard as eating the labour itself. He calls it defensible idiom; a minor.
